e: A Route 53 geoproximity routing policy directs users to the Region with resources closest to their location (adjustable with a bias), and a load balancer in each Region spreads traffic across the Availability Zones. Geolocation routes by user country rather than nearest, and multivalue or weighted policies ignore location.

RDS encryption at rest with KMS keys is a single setting, and SSL/TLS connections (with certificates) encrypt data in transit with minimal effort. IPsec tunnels, VPNs, or third-party application-level encryption add operational overhead.

An AWS Backup plan for RDS with 90-day retention (using continuous backup for point-in-time restore within the PITR window) meets both the 90-day retention and 14-day point-in-time recovery with centralized, automated management. Daily manual snapshots or automated backups alone can't give a 90-day retention, and Aurora cloning doesn't apply to RDS for Oracle.

Aurora Serverless is a relational managed database that scales capacity automatically with variable, read-heavy usage and bills for what is used, so it's the most cost-effective fit. Provisioned IOPS and magnetic storage waste money or perform poorly, and DynamoDB isn't relational.

A gateway endpoint keeps S3 traffic private, and an IAM policy that denies S3 access unless the resource belongs to the company's account (using a condition key such as aws:ResourceAccount) covers every customer bucket without listing each one, which is the least overhead. Listing specific buckets or using NAT gateways and per-bucket policies takes more effort.

IAM Identity Center permission sets with granular RDS and S3 access, assigned to groups for each team, centralizes least-privilege access with the least operational overhead and no individual IAM users. Per-team roles, IAM users, or separate accounts for each team add management.

IAM Roles Anywhere lets on-premises workloads use X.509 certificates to obtain temporary AWS credentials for an IAM role, giving the application secure, temporary access to the S3 bucket without long-term keys. Public IP bucket policies and stored access keys are less secure.

Attach the Direct Connect (through a Direct Connect gateway and transit VIF) to an AWS Transit Gateway shared with the other accounts, so all current and future accounts' VPCs get consistent, cost-effective access to the on-premises DNS and directory services with little operational work. A DX connection or VPN per account is costly and laborious.

A CloudFront distribution with the existing ALB as origin accelerates dynamic content worldwide using the AWS edge network and reuses connections to the origin, cost-effectively and with no redesign. S3 website hosting can't run a dynamic application, and Route 53 or Direct Connect don't provide global content delivery.

S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers as usage changes, saving money on data unused for months while keeping multi-AZ durability and availability and instant access. Standard costs more for idle data, Deep Archive isn't immediate, and One Zone-IA stores in a single AZ.

Amazon EFS is a highly available, regional shared file system that multiple instances in an Auto Scaling group can mount at the same time, with little change to application code. A single EBS volume can't be shared, an NFS server on EC2 is a single point of failure, and FSx for Windows in one AZ isn't a resilient Linux fit.

The application uses TCP, so a Network Load Balancer fits (the cheapest layer 4 option), and an Auto Scaling group automatically scales the EC2 instances as users increase and replaces unhealthy instances. ALBs are for HTTP, Gateway Load Balancers are for appliances, and manual scaling isn't automatic.

A tag policy in Organizations defines and enforces the allowed values (sensitive/nonsensitive) for the data sensitivity tag key, while service control policies deny launching instances without the tag and deny deleting tags, which tag policies alone can't do. Config with Lambda only reacts after the fact.

Set the RDS automated backup retention period to 30 days (the cheapest approach), which keeps the existing automated backups, and manually delete manual snapshots older than 30 days, since manual snapshots aren't removed automatically. Disabling automated backups would delete them, and AWS Backup adds cost.
Amazon EFS is a managed NFS file system that provides the NFS protocol the legacy application needs. DataSync is a transfer service, EBS is block storage, and EMRFS is for EMR.

An SQS queue durably stores incoming location data so it isn't lost during surges and the application can poll and process at its own pace, with little operational effort. S3 scanning, concurrent Lambda processing without a buffer, or polling DynamoDB don't provide the same replayable buffering.

Placing the RDS cluster in private subnets (not public) and using a Site-to-Site VPN from the office gives secure private connectivity for the desktop client without exposing the database to the internet. Public subnets or security-group-only access from the internet are less secure.

Data transferred between EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone (using private IPs) is free, whereas traffic across AZs or Regions is charged, so placing the instances in the same AZ minimizes transfer costs. Transfer between S3 and EC2 in the same Region is free.

AWS Secrets Manager stores the Aurora credentials encrypted with a KMS key and has built-in managed rotation for Aurora with a configurable schedule (14 days), requiring the least operational effort. Parameter Store, EFS, or S3 files need custom rotation code.

Video processing of terabyte files taking up to 20 minutes exceeds Lambda's 15-minute limit, so use containers on ECS with Fargate, which scale with demand without servers, and store content in S3 Intelligent-Tiering. EC2 fleets need management, and Deep Archive storage and single-AZ RDS aren't suitable.

EKS with AWS Fargate (a Fargate profile) runs pods on serverless compute with no nodes to manage, which fits the requirement not to manage the underlying compute with the least overhead. Self-managed nodes, managed node groups, and Karpenter on managed node groups still involve EC2 instances.

Aurora Serverless is a managed relational database that scales automatically with traffic, offers automated backups, and charges for capacity actually used, making it the most cost-effective option here. Self-managed databases add operations, and RDS doesn't have an on-demand capacity mode.

A gateway VPC endpoint for S3, with the subnet route table updated, sends the EC2 instance's S3 traffic over the AWS private network rather than the public endpoint. S3 buckets can't be moved into a VPC, access points don't change the network path, and Direct Connect isn't for VPC-to-S3 traffic.

The catalog is read-heavy and rarely updated, so caching it in ElastiCache for Redis (lazy loading) serves searches from memory and takes the load off the database CPU. Redshift is for analytics, scaling web servers doesn't reduce database load, and Multi-AZ or throttling doesn't improve performance.

A Volume Gateway with cached volumes stores the full data set in S3 (solving the limited local space) and keeps frequently accessed data in a local cache for low latency, presenting iSCSI block volumes to the on-premises applications. Stored volumes keep everything on premises, File Gateway is file-based, and Tape Gateway is for backup.
